query: rg mars|multivariate.adaptive in Analysis, Probability and LinearAlgebra; inspect SignedMeasure.totalVariation in VectorMeasure/Decomposition/Jordan.lean
result: No MARS complexity declaration appeared in the searched modules; totalVariation is the sum of the positive and negative Jordan measures and can be evaluated on the punctured coefficient domain.
comparisons: Evaluate each signed measure's totalVariation on the half-open cube with the all-zero atom removed, then sum over admissible interactions; whole-space variation would incorrectly penalize the unpenalized linear products, and descent from a representation to a function still needs justification.
gap: mathlib supplies signed-measure total variation, while the interaction-indexed punctured-domain sum and its representation-independent interpretation as MARS complexity remain to be defined and justified.

query: rg spherical|sphere.*measure|polar.*coord|surface.*measure|angular in MeasureTheory and Analysis; inspect withDensity and Real.cos
result: The search found planar polar-coordinate integration infrastructure, and withDensity constructs a measure from a nonnegative extended density; no inspected declaration gives this arbitrary-dimensional angular reference density with its printed cosine powers.
comparisons: The product of cosines and its normalization can be supplied to withDensity after restricting to the archived angular domain and proving nonnegativity and unit mass; its law is the fixed uniform-direction reference, not the observed angular marginal under an alternative.
gap: The density primitives are available, but the paper's angular domain, normalization and identification with the uniform-sphere reference law require a dedicated construction.

query: Inspect intervalIntegral in Integral/IntervalIntegral/Basic.lean and Real.sqrt in Analysis/Real/Sqrt.lean; search localized-statistic and kernel-estimator terminology in Probability and Analysis
result: The inspected declarations provide oriented real-time integration and the nonnegative real square root; no paper-specific Lambda tolerance correction was found in the searched estimator infrastructure.

gap: Time integration and square roots are available, but the kernel-path tolerance ratio and its source-specific denominator convention still need to be defined.

query: rg nadaraya|kernel.regression|kernel.estimat in Probability, Analysis and LinearAlgebra; inspect Finset.sum_div in Algebra/BigOperators/Field.lean
result: No Nadaraya-Watson or boundary-normalized marginal regression estimator appeared; Finset.sum_div supplies the finite-sum algebra for scaling the empirical numerator.

gap: Finite-sum scaling is available, while the boundary-normalized regression estimator and its unresolved zero-density convention require a paper-specific definition.

query: rg tensor.*contract|mode.*tensor and map_tprod; inspect PiTensorProduct/Basic.lean 469-487, Matrix.mulVec and Data/Holor.lean
result: PiTensorProduct.map applies a family of linear maps to tensor factors, and mulVec implements the coordinate contraction; Holor supplies coefficient arrays and outer products but the inspected file has no named k-mode contraction.
comparisons: Use the loading matrix as the linear map on factor k and identity maps elsewhere; the coefficient identity must match the printed left action U[j,i_k], changing only dimension k, rather than treating an abstract tensor product as already identical to the coefficient array.
gap: Tensor-factor maps and matrix-vector contraction are available; the paper's indexed-array k-mode product needs the coordinate identification and its entrywise correspondence.

query: rg tucker|tensor.factor|mode.product in Probability, Analysis and LinearAlgebra; inspect PiTensorProduct.map, Matrix.mul_apply and Holor coefficient-array operations
result: The tensor-factor hits concern algebraic tensor factors, not a stochastic Tucker factor model; indexed tensor maps and matrix multiplication provide the loading operations, without model assumptions.
comparisons: Apply one map per mode to the latent core and add the constant mean and noise tensor; the intercept is present in this source and cannot be dropped when grouping with the mean-free model.

The loading maps need full column rank as the paper assumes, not orthonormality; the abstract tensor map supplies the multilinear signal transformation but neither its latent time-series law nor the stated noise conditions.

For two positive factor counts, matrix multiplication represents R F C-transpose; the three printed zero-factor branches require separate definitions, since multiplying empty factor matrices would not yield the one-way models.
gap: mathlib provides the tensor and matrix loading operations, while the stochastic factor models, intercept and rank requirements, and explicit one-way or zero-factor branches need variant-specific definitions.

query: Inspect Matrix.mulVec, CFC.rpow, Independence/Basic.iIndepFun and Moments/Covariance.covariance; compare CovarianceBilin.covarianceOperator's explicitly uncentered convention
result: Matrix action and positive functional calculus support the two noise terms, independence predicates support indexed innovations, and scalar covariance can describe covariance-matrix entries; covarianceOperator is uncentered and cannot be used as centered covariance without a mean check.
comparisons: Construct each fiber as Psi_l e_t plus the positive square root of Sigma_l acting on epsilon_t,l; retain exactly the printed cross-family and cross-fiber independence, zero means, identity covariance, and dimension-uniform matrix bounds, without adding core-noise independence.
gap: Matrix action, square roots, covariance and independence primitives are available, but the fiber decomposition with its precise independence pattern and aggregate dimension bounds remains a separate model assumption.

query: rg linear.process|weakly.stationary in Probability and Analysis; inspect iIndepFun, IdentDistrib, covariance and InfiniteSum/Defs.lean 89-115
result: No named statistical linear-process declaration was found; joint independence and equal-law predicates are available, as are covariance and limits of partial sums, while InfiniteSum distinguishes unconditional and sequential summation conventions.
comparisons: The normalized absolutely summable filter must act on the factor innovations with the printed zero means and unit variances; construct the series in a justified convergence mode and retain identity within-fiber covariance and zero cross-fiber covariance, without upgrading zero covariance to independence.
gap: Independence, equal laws, covariance and convergence are available, while the filtered factor process, its convergence and the stated fiber covariance constraints need a dedicated construction.

query: rg factor.strength in Probability, Analysis and LinearAlgebra; inspect Matrix.PosDef, Filter.Tendsto and Asymptotics.IsLittleO
result: The inspected library contains positive-definite matrices, filter convergence and little-o growth, but no combined loading-factor-strength condition.
comparisons: Express the diagonal-normalized Gram limit and factor-count growth with separate dimension/sample filters, plus the positive-definite spectral bounds and ordered strength exponents; positive definiteness of an individual matrix does not supply uniform eigenvalue bounds for a growing sequence.
gap: Positive definiteness, limits and little-o growth are available, but the normalized Gram convergence and uniform spectral and power-growth requirements remain to be assembled with their original quantifiers.

query: rg linear.process|weakly.stationary in Probability and Analysis; inspect the iid predicates and InfiniteSum/Defs.lean's summation-filter conventions
result: The search did not identify a named weakly stationary error linear-process model; iid properties and partial-sum convergence can be expressed with the inspected general predicates.
comparisons: The two filters for common and idiosyncratic errors must separately satisfy l2 normalization and absolute summability; retain mutual independence between their innovation families and iid mean-zero unit-variance elements, while proving the chosen series construction and weak stationarity instead of assuming them from a totalized infinite sum.
gap: The iid and convergence primitives are available, while the two filtered error processes and their summability, covariance and stationarity properties require construction and proofs.

query: Inspect eLpNorm and MemLp in Function/LpSeminorm/Defs.lean for exponent 4 and the distinction between membership and a common bound
result: eLpNorm at exponent 4 measures the fourth absolute moment to the one-quarter power, while MemLp only asserts measurability and finiteness, not uniformity over a family.
comparisons: Apply a single finite upper bound to the fourth moments across every stated factor and error innovation index; separate MemLp 4 membership for each variable is weaker and neither Gaussian tails nor independence should be added to this member.
gap: mathlib supplies fourth-moment seminorms and integrability, while the single bound quantified uniformly over all three innovation families must be stated explicitly.

query: Inspect Set.pi and Set.powerset for optional Cartesian fiber subsets; compare PMF.uniformOfFintype with the source’s unspecified random-sampling law
result: Cartesian products and powersets of the finite index domain are available; a uniform finite law is constructible but the source passage does not specify uniformity or sample independence.
comparisons: Represent S_m either directly as a fiber-index subset or as the Cartesian product of coordinate subsets; keep sample-local sums and normalizations and do not infer uniform sampling, independence, or the full-population loading condition from this description.
gap: Subset and Cartesian-product infrastructure is available, but the paper's random subset scheme and sample-local estimators need definitions without inventing an unstated sampling law.

query: rg eigenvalue.ratio in Mathlib; inspect Spectrum.lean 277-281 and Matrix.mul_apply for the centered sample Gram matrix
result: The library's self-adjoint eigenvalues are already sorted in decreasing order; the search did not find the paper's sample-covariance ratio statistic.
comparisons: Form the centered sample covariance using the printed 1/T normalization and divide its largest eigenvalue by its j-th eigenvalue; translate one-based j to Fin indexing and retain unresolved zero-denominator cases rather than asserting the later asymptotic comparison from the definition.
gap: Ordered eigenvalues and matrix products are available, but the centered sample-covariance ratio needs its own definition and a source-consistent treatment of zero denominators.

query: rg pre.averag|eigenvalue.ratio in Mathlib; inspect ordered eigenvalues and eigenvectorBasis in Spectrum.lean and finite-sum scaling
result: The spectral API gives an orthonormal eigenbasis aligned with decreasing eigenvalues, and finite sums express averaged covariances; no selected-sample pre-averaging estimator was found.
comparisons: Select M samples by the stated eigenvalue ratios, average their centered covariances, and take z_k leading orthonormal eigenvectors; selection/eigenspace ties and zero signal normalization require explicit handling, and neither R2 nor L2-prime follows from this estimator definition.
gap: Ordered spectral bases and averaging algebra are available, while sample selection, the aggregate covariance estimator and signal rescaling require a dedicated construction with tie and denominator conventions.

query: rg stochastic.block|block.model across Mathlib and binomial in Combinatorics/SimpleGraph; inspect bernoulliMeasure and Measure.infinitePi
result: No stochastic-block-model declaration appeared; Bernoulli measures and indexed product measures construct independent binary edge variables for fixed parameters.

gap: Bernoulli product laws are available, but the shared-community multilayer model and symmetric loop-free adjacency encoding remain to be defined with conditional independence preserved.

query: Inspect Matrix.smul_apply and bernoulliMeasure's probability parameter; search stochastic-block-model terminology across Mathlib
result: Entrywise matrix scaling expresses the two coefficient matrices and Bernoulli parameters require membership in [0,1]; the specific assortative/disassortative alternatives were not found as a named model.
comparisons: Define the two 2-by-2 matrices with exactly the displayed diagonal/off-diagonal swap; rho in (0,2/3) proves all entries lie strictly between zero and one, and is not the same as permitting arbitrary symmetric layer matrices.
gap: Matrix scaling and Bernoulli laws suffice as primitives, while the two explicit alternatives and their probability-range checks still need to be defined.

query: Inspect uniformOfFintype, PMF.bind and bernoulliMeasure; search stochastic.block|block.model across Mathlib
result: Uniform distributions on nonempty finite types and probability mixtures are available, together with binary conditional edge laws; no balanced latent two-community multilayer model was identified.

gap: Finite uniform laws and mixtures are available, but the balanced latent model needs a specified prior coupling, conditional edge construction, and a clear distinction between joint and observation laws.
